other_mijikenda: Giriama, Duruma: Muhuhu (Pakia notes the name is shared by Digo, Duruma, Giriama and Swahili)

teaser.en: Second only to African blackwood for carving, this fragrant wood has become so scarce that carvers may cut only a few trees.

summary.en: *Muhuhu* is an evergreen tree of dry coastal forest whose hard, fragrant wood is second only to African blackwood for carving. Heavy cutting has made it Near Threatened, and mature trees now survive mostly in protected areas.

about.en: *Muhuhu* is an evergreen tree 8 to 15 metres tall, with branches that climb steeply upward. The leaves are spear-shaped, shiny above and covered in white felt below, so the tree flashes silvery-grey when the wind turns the leaves. The bark is grey and fibrous, peeling away in strips.

where.en: It grows in dry coastal forest and bushland. Mature trees are now scarce and are found mainly in protected areas.

uses.en:
Muhuhu is a carver's wood, second only to African blackwood. It is also used for flooring, and for poles and posts that resist termites.

A fragrant essential oil is distilled from the wood.

names.en: Pakia and the ICRAF handbook give the Digo name *muhuhu*, and Pakia notes it is shared by Digo, Duruma, Giriama and Swahili. In English it is also called muhuhu. The Mgombato dictionary gives a different Digo name, *mfufu*, 'silver oak', with Swahili *muhuhu*, and notes that woodcarvers use it extensively but are allowed only a limited number of trees.

conservation.en: Muhuhu is listed as Near Threatened on the IUCN Red List. Mature trees are now scarce and largely confined to protected areas, and carvers are allowed to use only a limited number.

reason.en: African blackwood, the only better carving wood
Its leaves are used to smooth carvings

definition.en: A hollow in the trunk, often at the knob left where a branch was cut. Pakia says this is common in muhuhu.

mgombato: mfufu (mi) silver oak (Brachylaena huillensis). A tall tree with grey-green foliage, used extensively by woodcarvers, who are allowed to use a limited number; muhuhu.
